scope: Proposition 3.1 (One-factor admissibility) of the manuscript “Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two” (preprints/Unrestricted-pro-modularity-at-the-prime-two-October-6-2026/two-adic-promodularity.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 010 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ef74b48557930663), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D be a complete noetherian local O-domain in which ϖ ̸= 0, and suppose that R → D is a finite continuous local map. Let L ̸= 0 be a finite torsion-free D-module with a commuting continuous right E(b)-action. Suppose that every copy of R acts through the same map R → D, and that M = Lb ⊗E(b) P(b) is admissible in the compact category. Then, using the first E-action, V = Lb ⊗EP is nonzero, O-torsion-free, and finite over A = O[[K]], for every sufficiently small uniform open subgroup K ⊂ SL2(Z2). It has a continuous commuting D-action.
